pentaho-community-edition.licensing_notes: Open-source software distributed under licenses such as Apache License 2.0, LGPL, and GPL.

faq.question: Is Pentaho Community Edition free for commercial projects?
faq.answer: Yes, as open-source software under licenses like Apache 2.0 and LGPL, it can be used commercially in compliance with open-source licenses.

faq.question: What is the primary difference between Pentaho Community and Enterprise editions?
faq.answer: The Enterprise edition includes proprietary modules and dedicated enterprise support. Consult the official documentation for details.

mule-community-edition.summary: Mule Community Edition (Mule Kernel) was an open-source integration runtime framework for connecting applications and data. MuleSoft has retired active updates for the open-source community edition.
mule-community-edition.what_it_does: Provided light enterprise service bus (ESB) messaging and integration runtime functions for connecting distributed software applications.
mule-community-edition.best_for: Organizations researching legacy MuleSoft open-source integration runtimes or evaluating enterprise integration patterns.
mule-community-edition.free_tier: Discontinued; active supported releases require a commercial enterprise license.
mule-community-edition.limitations: Community Edition is retired; current supported distributions require purchasing an enterprise license. Check official documentation for details.
mule-community-edition.licensing_notes: Discontinued open-source kernel; active supported versions require a commercial enterprise license from MuleSoft.

faq.question: Is Mule Community Edition actively maintained?
faq.answer: No, MuleSoft retired the open-source Mule Kernel; active supported releases require a commercial enterprise license.

faq.question: Where can I read current licensing options for MuleSoft products?
faq.answer: Current subscription terms and enterprise licensing options are available on the official MuleSoft website.
